why: Otherwise the filter/VC chain never initializes and the page loads empty.

rule: A filter dropdown's valueField = the raw KEY column downstream views filter on (name, period_id, participant_id); displayField = the human label.
why: Downstream views do WHERE key = :var; using a decorated label as the value returns no data.

rule: Dynamic / variable-column data => a `table` bound to the view, never a Custom card. N fixed-field richly-styled measure cards MAY be Custom at layoutSize 33.33.
why: Custom (controlData HTML) renders only a fixed, known field set.

rule: A dropdown that sets its own variable binds its default channel with [assignCurrentVariable, refresh].
why: Assign the current selection into the variable, then re-query.

rule: Every BIND channel must have a CREATE producer; a data control must subscribe every channel that sets a :param its view needs.
why: Dangling channels and unsatisfied params break the page and fail the gate.

rule: PageLoader: showLoader on $onPageLoad; hideLoader on an EARLY channel that always fires on load (the period/init-filter channel, e.g. current_period_select) — NOT the deepest chain channel; never a refresh handler.
why: Hiding on a deep channel (master_position_id, a table ready-signal) that may never complete leaves the loader spinning forever.

rule: Role/conditional sections use hidden:true by default and are revealed by a role variable.
why: e.g. show team components only for Manager/Leader.

rule: Reuse an existing catalog view before authoring; bind only real columns/params from the schema + catalog.
why: Avoids duplicate views and hallucinated columns.

rule: xc_participant & xc_position need effective-date overlap joins (xc_position also incent_st/end); banned: COALESCE/LEAST/GREATEST/IFNULL/LIMIT/Empty; no || in strict context.
why: These are the xSQL lint rules; obey up front.

rule: Use the same variable name for the same concept across all pages (v_period, v_master_participant_id, v_master_position_id, v_year_number).
Never invent a pageDefinitionId — it comes from the user's created page and is passed through verbatim.
why: A generated id orphans the page.

rule: Output convention: the design page is emitted as JSON; all datasource queries AND workflows are emitted as xSQL (.sql) files, not JSON envelopes.

Never use correlated subqueries or reference an OUTER alias inside a subquery JOIN...ON (Oracle ORA-00904 invalid identifier). Use single-level joins. For the position hierarchy use xc_position.parent_position_id (children) and a second self-join for grandchildren — not xc_pos_relations correlated COUNTs.
why: Xactly/Oracle cannot resolve outer correlations in a subquery ON clause; also a 504 risk.
